g10-economics-ue2-t1.overview: Theory of Demand sits inside Theories of Demand and Supply. Demand and supply are the focus of Unit 2 of Grade 10 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it builds the theory of demand, from the schedule and curve to the factors that shift demand. Then it does the same for the theory of supply. Next, it brings the two together to find market equilibrium, surpluses, and shortages. Finally, it measures elasticity: the price, cross, and income elasticity of demand, and the elasticity of supply. Students will also learn how demand and supply explain real-life prices and quantities.
objectives: Define demand and supply and state their laws.
Interpret schedules, functions, and curves for both.
Determine market equilibrium and identify surpluses and shortages.
Calculate the price, cross, and income elasticity of demand.
Compute and interpret the price elasticity of supply.
g10-economics-ue2-t1.simple:
Theory of Demand in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, demand as willingness plus ability to buy at a given price.
  • Then the demand schedule, the demand function Qd = a − bP, and the downward-sloping demand curve.
  • Also the factors that shift demand, such as income, related goods, tastes, and expectations.
  • Finally, the difference between a change in quantity demanded and a change in demand.
g10-economics-ue2-t1.detailed:
Theory of Demand — the essentials. First, demand as willingness plus ability to buy at a given price. Then the demand schedule, the demand function Qd = a − bP, and the downward-sloping demand curve. Also the factors that shift demand, such as income, related goods, tastes, and expectations. Finally, the difference between a change in quantity demanded and a change in demand.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Define demand and supply and state their laws.
  • Interpret schedules, functions, and curves for both.
  • Determine market equilibrium and identify surpluses and shortages.
  • Calculate the price, cross, and income elasticity of demand.
  • Compute and interpret the price elasticity of supply.

g10-economics-ue2-t3.simple:
Market Equilibrium in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, equilibrium where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied.
  • Then surpluses and shortages, and how they push the price back to equilibrium.
  • Also how a shift in demand or supply moves the equilibrium price and quantity.
g10-economics-ue2-t3.detailed:
Market Equilibrium — the essentials. First, equilibrium where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. Then surpluses and shortages, and how they push the price back to equilibrium. Also how a shift in demand or supply moves the equilibrium price and quantity.

  • Define demand and supply and state their laws.
  • Interpret schedules, functions, and curves for both.
  • Determine market equilibrium and identify surpluses and shortages.

  • Compute and interpret the price elasticity of supply.
